question.name: Q1
question.questiontext:
Please name the three frameworks of responsibility introduced in this course:

(Select three)

answer.answertext: Responsible Conduct of Research (RCR)
Collaborative Research (CR)
Peer Review (PR)
Research Misconduct (RM)
Responsible Research and Innovation (RRI)
Open Science (OS)

question.name: Q2
question.questiontext:
The RCR framework identifies a number of different areas of responsibility within research. Please select the three options below that ARE NOT included in the RCR framework:
(select three)

answer.answertext: Research misconduct
Protection of human subjects
Employment rights
Data management practice
Salaries and compensation
Conflict of interest and commitment
Collaborative research
Authorship and publications
Peer review
Career advice and progression

question.name: Q3
question.questiontext:
Creating responsible research environments is the responsibility of:

(Select one)

answer.answertext: The individual researcher
The institution
National research infrastructures
All options are correct

question.name: Q4
question.questiontext:
The Open Science movement emerged in response to a number of different pressures. Please select the five mentioned in the presentation that assisted in advancing the Open Science agenda:

(select five)

answer.answertext: The need for efficiency in research
More transparency in the use of public resources
Pressure from industry to commercialise research products
The emergence of citizen science and desire for further public engagement
Recognition of the importance of global research in response to the Sustainable Development Goals
Increased legislation around copyright and ownership of data
The need to increase the financial returns from research
Improve the speed of discovery

question.questiontext:

(select one)

answer.answertext: 1
6
8

Open Data

Open Access

Scientific Social Networks

Citizen Science

question.name: Q6
question.questiontext:
Please select the two sentences that describe the Open Science movement:

(select two)

answer.answertext: Open Science activities occur separately from responsible conduct of research activities
Different aspects of open behaviours occur at different stages throughout the research lifecycle
Openness in research is driven by different motivations to responsible conduct of research
Open Science activities are a progression and extension of responsible conduct of research activities
Openness in research requires that all resources be made maximally open at all times

question.name: Q7
question.questiontext:
Responsible Research and Innovation (RRI) was the third framework introduced in the presentation. Please select three elements that describe RRI:

(select three)

answer.answertext: Research should be co-produced with societal actors
Innovation products should be owned by societal actors
Innovation products should not be commercialised
Research and innovation products should reflect societal desirability
Research and innovation products should be socially acceptable and sustainable
Research ceases to be the responsibility of the researcher/research institution once it enters into innovation pathways

question.name: Q8
question.questiontext: Data stewards play an important role in safeguarding responsible research practices. Within the RCR framework they can actively work with researchers to discuss misconduct through data management and the implications of daily data decisions on research outputs. Select three practical actions mentioned in the presentation that data stewards can undertake to further RCR in their institution:

answer.answertext: Assist researchers with data management plans
Stop researchers from sharing data outside of institutional repositories
Provide legal advice on data sharing and copyright
Encourage researchers to regularly revisit and reflect on their data management plans
Undertake training and RCR advocacy

Form a link between data management practices within different institutions during collaborative projects

Research ceases to be the responsibility of the researcher/research institution once it enters into innovation pathways

question.name: Q9
question.questiontext:
While the Open Science landscape is developing rapidly, there is still much to be done to ensure unrestricted and equitable access to open research resources. There are a number of ways through which data stewards can assist in the development of the Open Science landscape. Select the three that were mentioned in the presentation:

(Select three)

answer.answertext: Always question how research can be made maximally Open and FAIR
Test Open Science platforms and tools
Ask about access to platforms and long-term sustainability
Develop their own Open Science tools

question.name: Q10
question.questiontext:
While RRI is a new framework of responsibility, there are a number of areas in which data stewards can assist in developing RRI cultures within their institutions. Select three such actions:

(Select three)

answer.answertext: Manage patent applications
Engage with innovators within institutions to discuss data management
Monitor institutional repositories to ensure responsible data re-use
Review copyright submissions
Ensure that curation supports RRI priority areas
Provide technical reviews of innovation products
Stop commercial use of institutionally-held datasets

question.name: Q1
question.questiontext: Data Stewards must have extensive domain-specific expertise (e.g., Social Sciences, Life Sciences).

answer.answertext: True
False
answer.feedback:
False. While many Data Stewards have strong research backgrounds and expertise in specific domains, others have expertise in research data management and curation more generally.


The focus areas of data stewards and mapping of different data steward roles
Image credit: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.3460552

question.name: Q2
question.questiontext:
Which of the following work areas may apply to the role of a Data Steward? 

Choose one answer.
question.generalfeedback:
Correct answer A. Data Stewards can be involved in a very broad range of research activities with some focusing more on policy development and interpretation; others focusing more on technical infrastructure provision; and others who are embedded in research teams and helping to define workflows and software.



Image credit: ‘RDM Skills’, Sarah Jones, https://www.slideshare.net/sjDCC/rdm-skills

answer.answertext: Policy development, providing training and guidance, defining research workflows, developing and managing research software, developing and delivery research infrastructure.
Policy development and providing training and guidance.
Developing and managing research software and developing and delivery research infrastructure
None of the answers are correct
Providing training and guidance

question.name: Q1
question.questiontext: FAIR data are always openly accessible.

answer.answertext: True
False
answer.feedback: Open and FAIR are not binary concepts and there can be degrees of both FAIRness and openness. Researchers need to consider exactly how much can be shared, at what points in the research lifecycle and with whom.

question.name: Q2
question.questiontext: Closed data can still be made FAIR.

answer.answertext: True
answer.feedback: There can be good reasons not to share data (e.g., to respect personal or commercial sensitivities) but in most cases there is something that can be shared such as the metadata description so that people at least know it exists and how they can go about requesting legitimate access.

answer.answertext: False

question.name: Q3
question.questiontext: Research data management only benefits others.

answer.answertext: True
False
answer.feedback: Good research data management is part of good research practice. RDM is vital to support research integrity and it also enables validation of published findings. Remember, that researchers often come back to reuse their own data so they may be the future reusers that benefit!

question.questiontext: How does EOSC Synergy support the vision of EOSC in practice?
